key_insight: UnDA enables cross-modal knowledge transfer in medical imaging without requiring paired data, using anchor-guided unpaired domain alignment to bridge large modality gaps. It also reduces error propagation by being more robust to uncertain source predictions.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of transferring knowledge between medical imaging modalities when paired clinical data is unavailable, and existing distillation methods fail under large modality differences and noisy source-domain outputs.
method: Uses anchor-guided unpaired domain alignment to connect source and target modalities without needing paired samples.
Aligns representations across modalities while accounting for large modality gaps.
Mitigates noise from uncertain source predictions to improve cross-modal knowledge transfer.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in medical imaging, UnDA offers a practical way to leverage multimodal information when paired datasets are scarce or impossible to obtain. This can improve downstream performance while making cross-modal transfer more reliable in real-world clinical settings.
visual_elements: Side-by-side source and target modality icons with an unpaired data gap between them
A pipeline diagram showing anchor-guided alignment from source to target
A comparison chart of paired vs. unpaired transfer methods
A noise-filter or confidence shield icon illustrating reduced error propagation
paper_title: UnDA: Unpaired Domain Alignment for Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer in Medical Imaging
paper_authors: Rafsan Jany, Shadab Tanjeed Ahmad, Ahsan Bulbul, Tahsinul Islam, Md Azam Hossain
